label: Can necessary abstracta and locally unreceived acts secure the same foundational bearer?
summary: C2 continuation of 71514b8a. See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md#testing-occupation-and-replacement. Pure sets can instantiate the finite cardinals without concrete members, leaving further dependence on nonmembers open. The singleton of n has the right rigid dependence but lacks independent warrant for necessity. In a populated order the closed-source and receptive-potency arguments give a local path from root access to an internally unreceived act under separate premises. The uncaused composite and isolated root distinguish inner receipt, external donation and common ancestry. Co-occupation of rival universal suppliers would violate their own role. Local uniqueness therefore cannot by itself exclude replacement. The prior warrant judgment stands. Van Cleve §§4 and 9 distinguish the isolation of n from the isolation of its companion and an originless companion from an order lacking n. The latter needs a separate reason to exclude their coexistence. Independent challenge reviewed the occupation analysis and its revision, then the affirmative branch at note blob 531f2445. Accepted repairs state the singleton assumptions, limit joint occupation to the same accessible worlds, and restrict the companion requirement to that route. The positive-conceivability test in docs/notes/foundational-absence-warrant.md distinguishes rigid identification, minimal realization and the literal claim of an exhaustive roster. Incomplete knowledge of n is no blanket defeater. The warrant for totality is the open burden. Independent semantic review accepted the roster analysis at 64ebcc34 under the same concrete-candidate interpretation of n.
blocker: Concrete accompaniment needs a reason independent of having finite-cardinal instances. Root access must apply at every relevant populated order. Rigid individuation must cover mutually exclusive occupants, or rigid dependence must be warranted for an independently necessary abstract witness. None of the models certifies a concrete-empty world or a same-n modal verdict.
